question.text: A cotton merchant enters forward sale at Rs 18,000/bale for April delivery. He buys a March 31 call option at strike Rs 17,500 with premium Rs 500. If cotton spot drops to Rs 16,000 on March 31, what is his net gain per bale?

answer.text: Rs 1,500 (forward sale revenue minus spot cost minus unexercised option premium)

explanation.text: The Logic: Forward sale price = Rs 18,000. Spot purchase = Rs 16,000. The call is not exercised because spot Rs 16,000 is below strike Rs 17,500. Premium paid = Rs 500. Net gain = 18,000 - 16,000 - 500 = Rs 1,500/bale. The Trap: Rs 2,000 ignores the premium. Rs 500 is just the premium. Rs 1,000 miscalculates. The call option was insurance — not needed since prices fell, but the premium remains a cost. Note: Had cotton risen above Rs 17,500, the merchant would have exercised the call to cap the buying cost — the option protects against an upside move in spot.
